nodes.description: Intellectual disability of variable severity. The disease concept is typically described as "moderate", but a molecularly characterised deletion case had an IQ below 40 (severe), so the grade is reported here with the generic term.

evidence.reference_title: Isolation of anonymous DNA sequences from within a submicroscopic X chromosomal deletion in a patient with choroideremia, deafness, and mental retardation.
evidence.snippet: We have recently identified two families in which choroideremia is inherited with mental retardation and deafness.

nodes.description: Deletion of further contiguous genes in the Xq21 segment beyond CHM and POU3F4 — mapping to the X-linked mental retardation (MRX) critical region between them (e.g. RPS6KA6/RSK4) and ZNF711 — underlies the intellectual disability, and (with obesity) distinguishes this syndrome from isolated choroideremia. The specific gene(s) responsible for obesity remain incompletely defined.

evidence.reference_title: A novel ribosomal S6-kinase (RSK4; RPS6KA6) is commonly deleted in patients with complex X-linked mental retardation.
evidence.snippet: RSK4 is completely deleted in eight patients with the contiguous gene syndrome including MRX, partially deleted in a patient with DFN3 and present in patients with an Xq21 deletion and normal intellectual abilities.

evidence.reference_title: A maternally inherited 8.05 Mb Xq21 deletion associated with Choroideremia, deafness, and mental retardation syndrome in a male patient.
evidence.snippet: POU3F4, CHM, and ZNF711 might have contributed to the patient's phenotype including hearing loss, poor vision, and intellectual disability

evidence.reference_title: Choroideremia and deafness with stapes fixation: a contiguous gene deletion syndrome in Xq21.
evidence.snippet: Two patients with deletions and choroideremia are affected by an X-linked mixed conductive/sensorineural deafness; one patient, XL-62, was confirmed at surgery to have DFN3

nodes.description: Deletion of POU3F4 (the DFN3 gene) removes a POU-domain transcription factor required for normal inner-ear (cochlear and middle-ear) development, causing X-linked mixed sensorineural and conductive hearing impairment, classically with stapes fixation and a perilymphatic "gusher" risk at surgery.

nodes.description: Centrifugal, progressive atrophy of the choriocapillaris, retinal pigment epithelium, and photoreceptors produces childhood-onset nyctalopia, progressive peripheral visual field constriction, and eventual central vision loss in affected males.

evidence.reference_title: Isolation of anonymous DNA sequences from within a submicroscopic X chromosomal deletion in a patient with choroideremia, deafness, and mental retardation.
evidence.snippet: Choroideremia, an X-chromosome linked retinal dystrophy of unknown pathogenesis, causes progressive nightblindness and eventual central blindness in affected males by the third to fourth decade of life.
Typically, symptoms in affected males evolve from night blindness to peripheral visual field loss, with central vision preserved until late in life.

nodes.description: Deletion of CHM eliminates Rab escort protein 1 (REP1), which presents Rab GTPases to geranylgeranyltransferase for prenylation. Defective Rab prenylation disrupts intracellular vesicular trafficking, especially in the retinal pigment epithelium and photoreceptors, leading to progressive degeneration of the choriocapillaris, RPE, and photoreceptor layer (choroideremia).

evidence.reference_title: Retinal degeneration in choroideremia: deficiency of rab geranylgeranyl transferase.
evidence.snippet: Lymphoblasts from choroideremia subjects showed a marked deficiency in the activity of component A, but not component B, of Rab GG transferase.

evidence.reference_title: Retinal degeneration in choroideremia: deficiency of rab geranylgeranyl transferase.
evidence.snippet: Rab geranylgeranyl transferase (GG transferase) is a two-component enzyme that attaches 20-carbon isoprenoid groups to cysteine residues in Rab proteins, a family of guanosine triphosphate-binding proteins that regulate vesicular traffic.

evidence.reference_title: A novel ribosomal S6-kinase (RSK4; RPS6KA6) is commonly deleted in patients with complex X-linked mental retardation.
evidence.snippet: The identification of deletions associated with classic CHM or DFN3 facilitated the positional cloning of the underlying genes, REP-1 and POU3F4, respectively

nodes.description: An interstitial deletion of the Xq21 region removes several contiguous genes, including the choroideremia gene CHM and the POU-domain transcription factor gene POU3F4 (DFN3), plus additional neighbouring loci in the X-linked mental retardation (MRX) region. The size and gene content of the deletion determine which extra-ocular features accompany the choroideremia.

evidence.reference_title: A maternally inherited 8.05 Mb Xq21 deletion associated with Choroideremia, deafness, and mental retardation syndrome in a male patient.
evidence.snippet: Deletions in Xq21 cause various congenital defects in males including choroideremia, deafness and mental retardation, depending on their size and gene content.

evidence.reference_title: A maternally inherited 8.05 Mb Xq21 deletion associated with Choroideremia, deafness, and mental retardation syndrome in a male patient.
evidence.snippet: The deleted region harbors 12 OMIM genes, of which POU3F4, CHM, and ZNF711 might have contributed to the patient's phenotype including hearing loss, poor vision, and intellectual disability.

evidence.reference_title: A novel ribosomal S6-kinase (RSK4; RPS6KA6) is commonly deleted in patients with complex X-linked mental retardation.
evidence.snippet: Large deletions in Xq21 often are associated with contiguous gene syndromes consisting of X-linked deafness type 3 (DFN3), mental retardation (MRX), and choroideremia (CHM).
